newsitem.title: FRANCE: France may legislate on work hours if no accord.
newsitem.headline: France may legislate on work hours if no accord.

text.p: The government will introduce legislation to curtail working hours if unions and employers fail to reach agreements by the end of the year, Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot said on Tuesday.
"If there are no results by the end of the year, we'll pass a parliamentary initiative in 1997," he said.

"For the moment, I don't see anything (happening)," he said. The government is pushing for voluntary accords to increase flexibility in work schedules to preserve jobs. The metals industry struck an accord last May entailing more paid leave in exchange for flexible scheduling.
